instructional_purpose: Establishes the top-level rhetorical partition between utterances that assert a state of affairs and utterances that enact something by being said, and trains the learner to sort utterance types into that partition even when the surface form points the other way. Serves as the organizing frame for the whole module.
concepts_taught: truth-evaluability as the criterion separating assertive from enacting utterances
validity/invalidity rather than truth/falsity as the verdict appropriate to enacting utterances
request-type enacting subtypes: command, prohibition, interrogation, wish, vocative, offer/urging
non-request enacting subtypes: oath, exclamation, set praise and blame formulas, contract formulas
particles that mark wish readings (ليت, عسى) and those that mark urging readings (هلّا، ألا، لولا، لوما)
first-person imperfective verbs whose utterance constitutes the act (pledging, accepting, promising, selling, marrying)
assertive form carrying directive force in asymmetric-authority speech
utterances that discharge both functions at once

linguistic_propositions.proposition: An utterance counts as assertive exactly when a true/false verdict can coherently be applied to its content; enacting utterances admit only a valid/invalid verdict.
A closed set of particles conventionally marks wish and urging readings and thereby signals an enacting clause.
Clauses with future or imperfective marking can carry directive force determined by speaker authority and situation rather than by any morphological marker.
First-person imperfective verbs from the pledging/accepting/promising/contracting lexical class denote the act performed by the utterance instead of describing an act.
Imperative morphology does not entail directive force; permission, indifference and threat readings are licensed by context.
An interrogative clause embedded under a knowledge verb belongs to the assertion that contains it and is not itself a request for information.
A single utterance may simultaneously carry assertive and enacting force, so the partition is not a disjoint labelling of tokens.

recognition_criteria: ask whether a true/false verdict fits the content; if it does not, the utterance is enacting
check for a dedicated wish/urging particle at the head of the clause
check for a first-person imperfective verb of the performative lexical class addressed to a hearer
check for an authority asymmetry in which the addressee's action is the expected uptake
check whether an interrogative is dominated by a knowledge or reporting verb
procedures: apply the truth-value test, then sort the enacting result into request-type versus non-request-type, then name the subtype
for a surface assertive, ask what act the speaker is performing before assigning force
for an oath, identify the swearing particle and treat the following clause as the sworn content
conditions: particle-based recognition holds only when the particle heads its clause
performative readings of first-person verbs require an addressee and a here-and-now utterance situation
directive readings of assertives require an authority or a fact that carries authority
exceptions: interrogative morphology inside an embedded knowledge clause is not a request
imperative morphology under permission or indifference readings is not a command
wish particles are not restricted to counterfactual content
contrasts: assertive versus enacting as the top-level split
request-type versus non-request-type enacting subtypes
grammatical form versus pragmatic function
genuine question versus rhetorical question

common_mistakes.pattern: treating every interrogative shape as a request for information
common_mistakes.why_wrong: an interrogative embedded under a knowledge verb reports what the speaker knows rather than asking anything
common_mistakes.correction_principle: check the syntactic environment of the interrogative before assigning it enacting force

common_mistakes.pattern: reading grammatical form as a direct index of function
common_mistakes.why_wrong: a future-marked clause can be a prediction or a command depending on the utterance situation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: assign force from context plus form, never from form alone

common_mistakes.pattern: assuming the wish particle always marks an impossible wish
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the same particle covers difficult-but-possible wishes and past-directed regret
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat impossibility as a frequent flavour, not a licensing condition

common_mistakes.pattern: treating every imperative shape as a command
common_mistakes.why_wrong: permission, concession, indifference and threat readings share the same morphology
common_mistakes.correction_principle: read the imperative against the speaker's stance toward the addressee's compliance

misleading_shortcuts: equating the presence of a wish or urging particle with a single fixed force, when لولا and لوما are shared with conditional and reproach constructions the lesson does not disambiguate
reading the truth-value test as a mechanical procedure applicable to running text
collapsing the two-way partition onto tokens when the lesson itself demonstrates dual-function utterances
worked_analysis_stages: identify the surface clause type
apply the truth-value test
name the enacting subtype if the test fails
read the pragmatic force against the speaker-addressee relation
note where form and function diverge
paradigms: two summary inventories are tabulated: request-type subtypes each paired with a canonical marker, and non-request subtypes each paired with a canonical marker or set formula; no inflectional paradigm is drilled
exercise_types: multiple choice on the defining criterion and on subtype naming
free-response recall of a subtype term
series fill-in classifying sample utterances as assertive or enacting
reuses_from_earlier: jussive command and prohibition morphology
interrogative particle inventory
oath particles and the genitive they assign
new_knowledge: the assertive/enacting partition as an organizing axis over utterances
the named subtype inventory of enacting speech
form-function mismatch as a systematic phenomenon rather than an oddity
later_dependencies: L5.M1.02 purposes of the assertive
L5.M1.03 emphasis calibration
L5.M1.04 assertive form with enacting force
any later work on rhetorical questions and negative-polarity idioms
sarf_relevance: low — touches only imperative and jussive shapes already established, with no new form derivation
nahw_relevance: medium — particle inventories, clause typing and embedding under knowledge verbs are parse-relevant, but the classification itself is pragmatic
tutor_drill_relevance: high — a clean binary sort with a named subtype layer supports graded drills, provided dual-function items are excluded or scored separately
rich_hover_relevance: medium — hovers on wish and urging particles gain from a force label, but the label must not be asserted from the particle alone
corpus_pvn_relevance: particle entries (p) dominate: the wish particles ليت and عسى, plus the urging set هلّا، ألا، لولا، لوما; noun entries (n) only for metalanguage terms; verb entries (v) for the performative senses of pledging/accepting/promising verbs
required_evidence: per occurrence: clause type, particle identity and position, presence of an embedding verb, and speaker-addressee relation; illocutionary force may not be projected from the particle or the verb form alone
uncertainty_flags: the truth-value test is a tradition-internal criterion, not a decision procedure over text
the lesson concedes dual-function utterances, which defeats single-label annotation
the urging particles are presented with one function each, though at least لولا and لوما are shared with conditional constructions

proposed_new_units.summary: A discriminator that separates assertive from enacting readings of a clause using surface-checkable features (head particle identity, imperative/jussive marking, first-person performative verb class, embedding under a knowledge verb) and explicitly abstains where only speaker-authority context could decide.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: The catalog units cover morphology, case/mood, governance and particle polysemy, but none assigns an utterance-level force label or records where force is underdetermined by form.

new_capability_required: speaker-authority and addressee-uptake features are unavailable to any current consumer; the non-particle cases would need a pragmatic-context interface before any force label could be projected

instructional_purpose: Teaches that an assertive utterance is produced for a purpose that need not be the transfer of new information, and supplies a named inventory of such purposes. Trains the learner to ask what the speaker is doing rather than only what the sentence says.
concepts_taught: the split between informing an ignorant addressee and signalling that the speaker shares what the addressee already knows
the notion of a rhetorical purpose distinct from propositional content
named purposes: warning, reproach, boasting, praise, lament, guidance, wonder, invocation, regret, appeal for mercy
assertive statements functioning as indirect refusal or indirect acceptance
contextual cues that reveal a purpose other than informing

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Assertive utterances divide by whether the addressee lacks the content (informing) or already possesses it (the speaker signalling shared knowledge).
The same assertive form may be produced to reject, warn, reproach, boast, praise, lament, guide or appeal, with no change to its grammatical shape.
Where the speaker has no plausible informing motive because the addressee manifestly already knows the content, the purpose must be sought elsewhere.
Perfective-form invocation and exclamation formulas are assertive shells whose purpose is non-informative.

recognition_criteria: ask whether the addressee could plausibly be ignorant of the content; if not, the purpose is not informing
look for mention of a hazard, a hostile party or an adverse consequence as a cue for a warning reading
look for a comparative or self-referential predicate as a cue for boasting or defence
read the relationship and relative standing of the interlocutors as part of the evidence
treat a statement of a defect in an object under evaluation as a refusal rather than a description
procedures: state the surface proposition, then ask what the speaker gains by uttering it here, then name the purpose from the inventory
separate the informing question (does the addressee know this?) from the purpose question (why say it?)
conditions: purpose assignment requires knowledge of what the addressee already knows
the warning reading requires a consequence the addressee can act on
the boasting or defence reading requires an implicit challenge to answer
exceptions: some assertives really are plain informing acts and need no further purpose ascribed
a purpose label may be layered rather than exclusive: an utterance can inform and warn at once
contrasts: informing versus signalling shared knowledge
surface proposition versus rhetorical purpose
description of a defect versus refusal
praise of a third party versus defence of one's own side

common_mistakes.pattern: assuming every assertive is a plain report of fact
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the grammatical form is constant across many purposes, so form gives no evidence about purpose
common_mistakes.correction_principle: recover purpose from the situation, not from the sentence shape

common_mistakes.pattern: conflating the informing purpose with the shared-knowledge purpose
common_mistakes.why_wrong: they are distinguished solely by whether the addressee already possesses the content
common_mistakes.correction_principle: test the addressee's prior knowledge before choosing between the two

common_mistakes.pattern: reading a statement of a problem as neutral description and missing the warning
common_mistakes.why_wrong: stating a hazard to someone who can be harmed by it is normally a caution
common_mistakes.correction_principle: when a stated fact bears on the addressee's exposure to harm, consider the warning reading first

common_mistakes.pattern: ignoring tone and interlocutor relationship
common_mistakes.why_wrong: identical wording praises or reproaches depending on standing and situation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat speaker-addressee relation as part of the evidence, not as background colour

misleading_shortcuts: treating the purpose inventory as a closed classification that must yield exactly one label per utterance
assuming any statement of a negative fact is automatically a warning
assuming that because a purpose can be named, it can be detected from text alone
worked_analysis_stages: state the surface content
assess the addressee's prior knowledge
name the operative purpose
state the action or attitude the purpose is meant to produce
paradigms: a purpose-to-effect table pairing each named rhetorical purpose with the practical upshot it aims at; no morphological paradigm
exercise_types: multiple choice selecting the operative purpose for a given utterance
multiple choice on the informing versus shared-knowledge distinction
free-response vocabulary and term recall
fill-in completing the pair of primary purposes
reuses_from_earlier: L5.M1.01 assertive/enacting partition
L5.M1.01 observation that form and function can diverge
new_knowledge: the two-way split of assertive purpose by addressee knowledge state
a named inventory of rhetorical purposes for assertive clauses
cues that a stated fact is functioning as refusal or caution
later_dependencies: L5.M1.03 emphasis calibrated to the addressee's stance, which presupposes modelling the addressee
L5.M1.04 assertive form with enacting force
sarf_relevance: none — no morphological content is developed
nahw_relevance: low — the lesson holds syntax constant on purpose and varies only the pragmatic layer
tutor_drill_relevance: medium — purpose-labelling drills are feasible only with a supplied situation, since the sentence alone underdetermines the answer
rich_hover_relevance: low — nothing here attaches to a token; the unit of analysis is the utterance in a situation
corpus_pvn_relevance: weak: noun entries (n) for the metalanguage purpose terms only; no particle or verb entries follow from the lesson's substance
required_evidence: per occurrence: the addressee's prior knowledge state, the interlocutors' relative standing, and the discourse move being answered; none of these are recoverable from the sentence string
uncertainty_flags: purpose labels are interpretive and admit multiple simultaneously correct answers
the informing/shared-knowledge split rests on an unobservable epistemic state

proposed_new_units.summary: A named taxonomy of purposes an assertive utterance can serve, together with the situational cues the tradition associates with each, held explicitly as teaching material rather than as a projection capability.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: No catalog unit ranges over utterance purpose, and the substance cannot be reduced to any of the five consumer-backed capability families because its decisive features are extralinguistic.

new_capability_required: addressee-knowledge-state modelling; no current consumer accepts a feature representing what the addressee already knows, which is the pivot of the entire lesson

instructional_purpose: Presents the inventory of devices that strengthen an assertive claim and ties the number of devices used to the addressee's assumed epistemic stance. Trains calibration: matching emphasis to actual resistance rather than applying it uniformly.
concepts_taught: three assumed addressee stances: unprepossessed, hesitant, denying
graded emphasis: zero devices, one device, two or more devices
إنّ as the primary emphatic particle on a nominal clause
لام التوكيد prefixed to the predicate of إنّ and to verbs under an oath
قد before a perfective verb as confirmation of realisation
نون التوكيد in heavy and light shapes suffixed to verbs
the oath as a maximal-credibility device
lexical repetition as the oldest emphasis device, in exact, synonymous and phrasal shapes
إنَّما as emphasis combined with exclusion
intensification of a claim in proportion to denial

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The quantity of emphasis a claim carries is licensed by the addressee's assumed stance: none for the unprepossessed, one device for the hesitant, two or more for the denier.
لام التوكيد attaches to the predicate of إنّ, and separately to a verb following the oath-lam.
قد before a perfective verb asserts that the event was realised.
قد before an imperfective verb is ambiguous between an emphatic and an epistemic-possibility reading, resolved only by context.
The emphatic nun forces a fatḥa on the verb's final radical and displaces the ordinary indicative or jussive ending.
The emphatic nun occurs on jussive- and subjunctive-marked verbs, in oath complements and in emphatic imperatives.
Lexical repetition of a word or phrase functions as emphasis in its own right.
إنّ and إنَّما differ in that only the latter adds exclusion of alternatives.

recognition_criteria: count the emphatic devices present in a clause and read off the assumed addressee stance
identify لَـ on the predicate of a nominal clause headed by the emphatic particle
identify قد immediately before a finite verb and check the verb's aspect
identify a fatḥa-plus-nun ending on a verb as the emphatic nun rather than a plural or feminine marker
identify a repeated lexeme in adjacent position as emphasis rather than as a coordination error
procedures: assess the addressee's stance, then select zero, one, or two-plus devices accordingly
to raise emphasis one step, add the emphatic particle; to raise it again, add the emphatic lam to the predicate; to raise it further, prefix an oath
to attach the emphatic nun, place a fatḥa on the verb ending before suffixing the nun
conditions: the emphatic lam is licensed on the predicate of the emphatic particle, not freely on any predicate
the emphatic nun requires the fatḥa-marked stem shape rather than the plain indicative or jussive ending
the confirmation reading of قد is primary with perfective verbs
exceptions: emphasis applied to an addressee with no doubt is rhetorically defective even though grammatical
the possibility reading of قد with imperfective verbs falls outside the emphatic function
the lesson illustrates the emphatic nun only on sound singular forms; dual, plural and weak stems undergo further adjustments not covered
contrasts: bare assertion versus one-device versus multi-device emphasis
emphatic particle versus emphatic-plus-exclusive particle
قد with perfective versus قد with imperfective
heavy versus light emphatic nun
exact repetition versus synonym repetition

common_mistakes.pattern: applying emphasis to an addressee who has no doubt
common_mistakes.why_wrong: emphasis presupposes resistance, so unmotivated emphasis wrongly imputes skepticism to the hearer
common_mistakes.correction_principle: match device count to actual resistance, treating zero as the correct value for a neutral hearer

common_mistakes.pattern: using the emphatic particle and the emphatic-exclusive particle interchangeably
common_mistakes.why_wrong: only the second excludes alternatives; substituting it changes the claim, not just its force
common_mistakes.correction_principle: ask whether alternatives are meant to be excluded before choosing the exclusive form

common_mistakes.pattern: reading قد with an imperfective verb as necessarily emphatic
common_mistakes.why_wrong: with imperfective verbs the particle also carries an epistemic-possibility reading
common_mistakes.correction_principle: let aspect and context select the reading; treat the emphatic reading as default only with perfective verbs

common_mistakes.pattern: suffixing the emphatic nun without adjusting the verb ending
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the emphatic nun replaces the indicative vowel or the jussive sukun and requires a fatḥa before it
common_mistakes.correction_principle: derive the emphatic form from the stem plus fatḥa plus nun, not by appending the nun to the inflected form

misleading_shortcuts: treating the device count as a rule rather than a teaching heuristic, so that two devices are read as proof of a denying addressee
generalising the emphatic-nun morphology shown on sound singular verbs to duals, plurals and weak stems
reading the emphatic lam as freely attachable to any predicate rather than licensed by its host particle
treating any clause-initial emphatic particle as evidence about the real hearer rather than the hearer the speaker assumes
worked_analysis_stages: identify the emphatic devices present
count them
infer the addressee stance the speaker is assuming
state what the emphasis is answering
paradigms: a stance-to-device-count table pairing each assumed addressee stance with the expected number of devices
a device inventory table pairing each emphasis device with its host category and attachment position
heavy and light emphatic-nun shapes contrasted on the same verb
exercise_types: multiple choice identifying a device or naming the addressee stance
multiple choice on the function of a specific particle
free-response recall of device names
series fill-in matching addressee stance to device count
prerequisite_knowledge: nominal sentence structure and its predicate slot
the emphatic-accusative particle and its case assignment
indicative, subjunctive and jussive verb endings
reuses_from_earlier: L5.M1.01 oath as an enacting subtype, now reused as an emphasis device
nasikh particle governance from earlier case work
verb mood endings
new_knowledge: the addressee-stance scale as the licensing condition for emphasis
the consolidated emphasis-device inventory with attachment positions
the emphatic nun's effect on the verb's final vowel
the aspect-sensitivity of قد
later_dependencies: L5.M1.06 exclusive restriction, which builds on the emphatic-plus-ما form introduced here
L5.M1.05 amplification, which reuses repetition as a device
any later work on oath complements and their verb forms
sarf_relevance: medium — the emphatic nun genuinely alters the verb's final vowel and ending class, which is inflectional morphology rather than rhetoric
nahw_relevance: high — device attachment is licensed by host category and clause position, and the emphatic particle's case assignment is presupposed throughout
tutor_drill_relevance: high — device identification and stepwise emphasis-raising are both mechanically checkable; the stance inference is not
rich_hover_relevance: high — قد، لَـ، إنّ and the emphatic nun are all token-level and all polyfunctional, so hovers need a licensing note rather than a single gloss
corpus_pvn_relevance: particle entries (p) for قد، إنّ، إنَّما, for لام التوكيد and نون التوكيد, and for the oath particles; verb entries (v) wherever the emphatic nun changes a surface form that must be linked back to its lemma; noun entries (n) only for metalanguage
required_evidence: per occurrence: host category of the device, its position relative to predicate or verb, verb aspect for قد, and the verb's ending shape for the emphatic nun; the addressee-stance claim requires discourse evidence and should not be projected
uncertainty_flags: the device-count scale is a didactic heuristic, not a licensing rule
the emphatic reading of قد with imperfective verbs is contested and context-bound
emphatic-nun morphology beyond sound singular verbs is not covered and must not be inferred from the examples given

proposed_new_units.summary: A table stating, for each emphasis device, what category it attaches to, in what position, and what co-occurrence it requires: the emphatic lam licensed on the predicate of the emphatic particle or under the oath-lam; the emphatic nun licensed on jussive/subjunctive verbs with an obligatory fatḥa; قد licensed pre-verbally with aspect-dependent readings.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 covers the nasikh particles' governance and u-s09 covers inflectional layering, but neither records cross-device attachment licensing or the co-occurrence stacking that this lesson makes central.

instructional_purpose: Isolates the case where a grammatically assertive clause performs an act, and gives it named subtypes with recognition cues. The pedagogically load-bearing case is perfective-form invocation, where the tense form must not be read as past reference.
concepts_taught: assertive form with enacting function as a distinct third category
assertive functioning as a directive when the speaker or the stated fact carries authority
first-person assertive about future action functioning as an irrevocable commitment
assertive about a completed task functioning as a claim to a new role
perfective-form invocation formulas expressing supplication rather than past reference
second-person predicate-nominal assertive conferring the status it names
why assertive framing outranks explicit command in force

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Perfective-form clauses with the divine name as subject, drawn from a small set of invocation lexemes, express supplication rather than past reference.
A past-time adverbial in the same clause blocks the supplication reading and restores the past-reporting reading.
A first-person assertive about future action with no epistemic hedge functions as a commitment rather than a prediction.
An assertive uttered by a party with authority, stating a condition that bears on the addressee, carries directive force.
A second-person clause with a predicate nominal may enact the status it predicates rather than describe an existing one.
Assertive framing is more coercive than an explicit imperative because it locates the necessity in the facts rather than in the speaker's will.
Not every assertive carries hidden enacting force; the default reading remains plain report.

recognition_criteria: for supplication: perfective verb from the invocation lexeme set, divine name as subject, no past-time adverbial, and a context of illness, death or blessing
for commitment: first-person subject, future or ongoing aspect, absence of hedging particles
for directive: statement of an obstacle or condition, speaker with standing, addressee action as the expected uptake
for status conferral: second-person subject with a predicate nominal naming a role, uttered by someone entitled to confer it
absence of any of these cues supports the plain-report default
procedures: state the grammatical form, then state the function, then state the speaker's intent as a separate line
run the indicator checklist for each of the four subtypes before defaulting to plain report
for a perfective clause, test for a past-time adverbial before assigning the supplication reading
conditions: the directive reading requires an authority differential or facts that carry their own authority
the commitment reading requires the absence of possibility-hedging particles
the supplication reading requires the invocation lexeme set and the absence of past-time anchoring
exceptions: the same invocation formula with an explicit past-time adverbial is a genuine past report
a subordinate speaker uttering an authority-typed assertive is reporting, not commanding
plainly descriptive assertives with no situational stake carry no enacting force
contrasts: assertive form with enacting function versus overtly enacting form
perfective-as-supplication versus perfective-as-report
explicit imperative versus assertive directive, compared on coercive force
explicit role claim versus implicit role claim through reporting a completed task

common_mistakes.pattern: treating every assertive as a pure report
common_mistakes.why_wrong: assertive shape is compatible with directive, commitment, status-claim and supplication functions
common_mistakes.correction_principle: ask what act the utterance performs before recording it as a report

common_mistakes.pattern: reading a perfective invocation formula as a statement about the past
common_mistakes.why_wrong: these formulas are optative in force despite perfective morphology
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use the past-time-adverbial test: its absence in an invocation context supports the supplication reading

common_mistakes.pattern: ignoring the standing of the speaker
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the directive reading of an assertive depends on who may impose on whom
common_mistakes.correction_principle: assign the directive reading only where the speaker or the stated fact has authority over the addressee

common_mistakes.pattern: reading hidden performative force into ordinary descriptive statements
common_mistakes.why_wrong: over-application makes the category vacuous
common_mistakes.correction_principle: require a positive contextual cue before departing from the plain-report default

misleading_shortcuts: treating perfective morphology as a reliable index of past reference across the board
treating any statement of a problem as a covert command regardless of who is speaking
assuming the four subtypes exhaust the possibilities or are mutually exclusive
assuming the absence of an explicit imperative means no directive was issued
worked_analysis_stages: state the grammatical form
state the pragmatic function
state the speaker's intent and the intended uptake
note which cue licensed the departure from the plain-report reading
paradigms: a form-to-function table pairing assertive shapes with their enacting readings
a closed list of fixed invocation formulas built on perfective verbs plus the divine name
three indicator checklists, one per enacting subtype
exercise_types: multiple choice distinguishing form from function
multiple choice assigning the enacting subtype
free-response term recall
series fill-in classifying sentences as plain report or assertive-with-enacting-force

L5.M1.02 purpose inventory, of which invocation and guidance recur here

proposed_new_units.summary: A discriminator deciding, for a perfective verb from an enumerated invocation set with a divine-name subject, whether the clause is optative or past-referring, keyed on subject identity, lemma membership and the presence of a past-time adverbial; abstains outside the enumerated set.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: No catalog unit maps a verb form to a non-default temporal or modal reading; the sarf units classify templates and the nahw units classify case, mood and structure, none of which records this form-to-force override.

proposed_new_units.summary: The directive, commitment and status-conferral readings of assertive clauses, retained as teaching material with their indicator checklists but explicitly not projectable.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: Their decisive features are authority relations and discourse stakes, which no consumer-backed capability family can represent.

instructional_purpose: Introduces the length axis of expression: saying less than expected, saying more than expected, and the neutral midpoint, each with named subtypes. The syntactically load-bearing parts are the ellipsis type of brevity and the parenthetical-insert type of amplification.
concepts_taught: the three-way length scale: brevity, parity, amplification
brevity without omission versus brevity through ellipsis
recovery of an omitted head from context in the ellipsis type
five amplification techniques: repetition, synonym-piling, elaboration after a summary, parenthetical insertion, confirming appendage
the removability test for identifying a parenthetical insert
register correlation: brevity signalling authority, amplification signalling deference and persuasion

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Brevity divides into a compact-but-syntactically-complete type and an elliptical type, distinguished by whether a recoverable element is absent.
A recurrent ellipsis type deletes a governing head noun while its dependent remains in place, obliging the reader to restore the head to obtain the intended sense.
A parenthetical insert occupies a position between subject and predicate and can be removed without leaving the remaining clause ungrammatical.
Amplification is realised by an enumerable set of techniques, each identifiable by the relation between the added material and what it expands.
Synonym-piling and exact repetition are distinct techniques, separated by whether the repeated material is the same lexeme or a near-synonym.
Choice of length register correlates with the speaker's social role and communicative aim rather than with propositional content.
A short sentence is not automatically of the non-elliptical brevity type; shortness and completeness are independent.

recognition_criteria: for the ellipsis type: ask whether a constituent must be supplied for the clause to mean what it evidently means
for the deleted-head pattern: a dependent whose semantics do not fit the overt head signals a missing head
for a parenthetical insert: test whether deleting the span leaves a well-formed clause, and check for invocation content set off by dashes or commas
for synonym-piling: two or more coordinated near-synonymous predicates or nominals in sequence

instructional_purpose: Teaches restriction as a device that affirms one element while implicitly excluding all alternatives, using the emphatic particle extended by ما. Combines a real case-marking consequence with a focus-position account of which element is restricted.
concepts_taught: restriction as simultaneous affirmation and implicit exclusion
the composition of the restrictive particle from the emphatic particle plus ما
suspension of the emphatic particle's accusative government by the attached ما
the nominative subject that results from that suspension

the implicit negation that every restricted clause carries
equivalence in force with the negation-plus-exception construction and with fronting

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The ما attached to the emphatic particle blocks that particle's accusative government, so the following subject appears in the nominative.
The restrictive particle affirms one element and implicitly negates the alternatives.
The element in delayed position is the focus of restriction, and reordering the clause changes what is restricted.
Restriction comes in two directions, named after which predication role is restricted to the other.
The restrictive particle is followed by a subject-predicate nominal clause.
The negation-plus-exception construction is truth-conditionally equivalent to the restrictive particle, differing only in explicitness.
Fronting an element that would ordinarily follow implies restriction to that element.

recognition_criteria: identify the restrictive particle at the head of a clause
check the case of the following nominal: nominative rather than accusative confirms the suspension of government
identify which element occupies the final position to determine the focus of restriction
state the excluded set explicitly to confirm a restrictive reading was intended
distinguish the restrictive particle from the bare emphatic particle by the presence of ما and the case outcome
procedures: to read a restricted clause: name the particle, assign case, locate the delayed element, then state the implicit negation
to determine the restriction direction: identify the two predication roles and ask which one is being confined to the other
to convert a restricted clause into its negation-plus-exception equivalent, negate the clause and except the focused element
conditions: the nominative outcome is conditioned on the ما being the government-blocking type rather than a negator or relative
the focus rule presupposes that the clause has a manipulable order
the exclusion reading presupposes that alternatives were live in the discourse
exceptions: the lesson's own examples include the restrictive particle followed by a verb-initial clause, which the stated subject-predicate template does not cover
the emphatic particle without ما assigns the accusative, so the case outcome is not a property of the particle stem alone
contrasts: emphasis alone versus emphasis plus exclusion
accusative subject under the bare particle versus nominative subject under the extended particle
the two directions of restriction, distinguished by which element is delayed
restrictive particle versus negation-plus-exception versus fronting, as three routes to the same force

common_mistakes.pattern: using the emphatic particle and the restrictive particle interchangeably
common_mistakes.why_wrong: only the restrictive form excludes alternatives, so the substitution changes the proposition
common_mistakes.correction_principle: choose the restrictive form only when alternatives are genuinely meant to be excluded

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning the accusative to the subject after the restrictive particle
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the attached ما suspends the particle's government, leaving the nominative
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat the case outcome as diagnostic of which particle is present

common_mistakes.why_wrong: the direction of restriction is read off the delayed element, so mistaking it inverts the claim
common_mistakes.correction_principle: locate the final element first, then name the direction

instructional_purpose: Teaches the second route to restriction: negate the whole, then except one element. Carries the module's densest case-assignment content, since the excepted element's marking depends on whether the general term is overt.
concepts_taught: negation followed by exception as an explicit restriction structure
the negators that can head the construction and the clause types each suits

emptied exception, where the general term is unexpressed

the terminology of excepted element and general term

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Under the emptied exception, the excepted element takes the case its grammatical role in the clause requires, so the outcome may be nominative, accusative or genitive.
With an overt general term in an affirmative clause, the excepted element is accusative by exception.
With an overt general term in a negated clause, the excepted element may be accusative by exception or may follow the general term's case as a substitute, and both are licensed.
The exception particle is not a coordinator: it withdraws one element from a negated whole rather than adding a further element.
Under the categorical negator, the negated noun is built on fatḥa while occupying an accusative slot, and the excepted proper noun is nominative as a substitute for that slot.
Different negators are distributed across clause types: some suit nominal clauses, one suits negated past verbs, one marks categorical negation.
The negation-plus-exception route is more explicit and more confrontational than the single-particle route, though truth-conditionally equivalent.

recognition_criteria: locate a negator and an exception particle in the same clause
check whether a general term intervenes between them to decide complete versus emptied
under the emptied type, determine the excepted element's grammatical role and assign case from that role
under the categorical negator, expect a built form on the negated noun and read the following nominative as a substitute
distinguish the exception particle from coordinators by asking whether the following element is withdrawn from a negated set
procedures: identify the negator, then check for an overt general term, then assign case by the applicable branch
for the emptied type, mentally delete the negator and exception particle and read off the case the remaining clause would assign
for the negated complete type, state both licensed case options rather than choosing arbitrarily
conditions: the emptied type is defined by the absence of an overt general term before the exception particle
the substitution option is available only under negation, not in affirmative complete exception
role-based case assignment presupposes that the governing element reaches past the exception particle
exceptions: the accusative is not automatic after the exception particle; under the emptied type it is only one of three possible outcomes
the negated complete type admits two analyses rather than one
contrasts: complete versus emptied exception
affirmative versus negated complete exception, which differ in the options available
accusative by exception versus case by substitution
negation-plus-exception versus the single restrictive particle, compared on explicitness

common_mistakes.pattern: confusing the emptied type with the complete type
common_mistakes.why_wrong: they are distinguished by whether a general term is overt, and they trigger different case rules
common_mistakes.correction_principle: look for an overt general term before the exception particle before applying any case rule

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning the accusative automatically after the exception particle
common_mistakes.why_wrong: under the emptied type the case follows the element's grammatical role, which may be subject or object of a preposition
common_mistakes.correction_principle: derive the case from the role, not from the particle

common_mistakes.pattern: treating the exception particle as a coordinator
common_mistakes.why_wrong: it withdraws one element from a negated set rather than adding a further member
common_mistakes.correction_principle: read the construction as negation of a whole followed by reinstatement of one member

common_mistakes.pattern: reading the construction as a bare affirmation and missing the exclusion
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the force of the structure lies in what the negation has swept away, not only in what is excepted
common_mistakes.correction_principle: always state the excluded set when analysing the construction

misleading_shortcuts: treating the exception particle as governing the accusative in all environments
assuming the two-option case outcome under negated complete exception is a free variation with no analytical consequence
assuming that because both restriction routes are equivalent in force they are interchangeable in register
reading the categorical-negator construction's marking as ordinary accusative rather than as a built form occupying an accusative slot

instructional_purpose: Turns the two restriction devices from objects of analysis into instruments of composition: converting general propositions into restricted ones, choosing between the devices by register, and analysing official prose for restriction scope. Runs the module's analytic content in the production direction.
concepts_taught: conversion of a general proposition into a restricted one
the semantic consequence of that conversion: from membership to exclusivity
register-based selection between the subtle and the explicit restriction device
word-order adjustment so the intended element occupies the focused slot

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Converting a general proposition into a restricted one changes the claim from membership in a class to exclusive identity with it, and can turn a true statement into a false one.
To restrict to a given element, that element must occupy the delayed slot; changing the order changes what is restricted.
Selection between the two restriction devices is a register and stance choice, not a truth-conditional one.
The explicit device suits legal drafting, rebuttal and confrontation; the implicit device suits general assertion and persuasion.
Restriction in official drafting fixes the scope of an obligation and the boundary of an exemption, eliminating the ambiguity a plain assertion leaves.
Every restricted proposition carries an implicit negation that the writer is committed to, whether or not it was intended.

recognition_criteria: scan for a clause-initial restrictive particle or for a negator paired with an exception particle inside a clause
identify what precedes the marker and what occupies the focused position
state the excluded set to make the commitment explicit
in official prose, read a restriction marker as delimiting either a scope or an exemption
detect layering when both devices appear across adjacent clauses of the same passage
procedures: identify the two predication roles, decide which is to be confined to the other, then apply the chosen device with the order that puts the target in the focused slot
select the device by register: implicit for calm assertion and wisdom, explicit for argument, rebuttal and legal text
analyse a document in three steps: locate the marker, identify what is restricted to what, state the implicit negation
for a scope clause use the implicit device with the action and its domain; for an exemption clause use a negator over the general category with the excepted category after the exception particle
conditions: restriction should be applied only where exclusion of alternatives is actually intended
device selection is conditioned on the communicative setting, not on the proposition
the order adjustment is required whenever the default order would focus the wrong element
exceptions: a proposition that is true as a general claim may become false under restriction, so the conversion is not always available
not every statement calls for restriction; the plain assertion remains the default
contrasts: general versus restricted proposition
the implicit device versus the explicit device, compared on register and force
restricting to the subject versus restricting to the predicate, distinguished by order
scope clause versus exemption clause in official drafting

common_mistakes.pattern: applying restriction where only assertion was meant
common_mistakes.why_wrong: restriction commits the writer to excluding every alternative, which is a much stronger and often false claim
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use restriction only when the exclusion is intended and defensible

common_mistakes.pattern: choosing the device that mismatches the setting
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the explicit device reads as combative in a reflective passage and the implicit device reads as vague in a legal clause
common_mistakes.correction_principle: select the device from the register before drafting

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the default order in place after choosing the device
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the restriction lands on whichever element occupies the focused slot, so the wrong order restricts the wrong element
common_mistakes.correction_principle: place the intended target in the delayed slot as part of applying the device

common_mistakes.pattern: not articulating the implicit negation
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the writer remains committed to the exclusion whether or not it was noticed
common_mistakes.correction_principle: state the excluded set aloud before accepting a restricted formulation

assuming restriction always sharpens a claim, when it can falsify it
treating the register guidance as a rule rather than as tendency drawn from illustrative prose
assuming the delayed-slot focus rule transfers unchanged from one device to the other without checking the resulting structure
